summary: A write made through the browser must evict the client's cached reads, and `reports exceptions` must always read live; the browser flows bypass the only code that clears the response cache.
reason: The response cache holds GETs for five minutes and is cleared only after a successful API mutation, but every browser fallback saves through Concur's web form instead. A read made soon after an edit (reports get, expenses list, reports exceptions) therefore returned the pre-edit state, including a blocking error that had just been fixed. An edit made in the web UI can never evict the cache, so the validation view skips it altogether.
validated_outcome: go build, go vet and go test ./... pass. Each browser-write flow's success-path test plants a cached response and asserts it is gone afterwards, and a live-read test asserts that `reports exceptions` reaches the server on every call; all six fail when the fix is removed. Found live: after `expenses update --type` cleared a line's blocking error, `reports exceptions` and `reports get` kept reporting it for several minutes until `--no-cache` was passed.
